beats.role_note: Game, the state the effect communicates, the objects (incl. the textured one); the colour line in the spec (CHANGE-BRIEF.md §1.1, §1.4).
beats.narration_text: The game is Vidiyum Mun, a time loop at a beach party in Chennai. Holding T at night runs the clock eight times faster, and whatever happens meanwhile goes unheard. The spec names that state exactly, and the colour line from the brief: mix the bar's colour toward sodium orange, by skip amount times tint strength. The textured shader goes on the four pool-deck floors: three dry, one wet.

beats.role_note: Q1 what a shader does: night_skip.gdshader, typed by Shriram. Paired result B04.
beats.narration_text: Here's the shader Shriram typed in. Shader type canvas item: it runs on 2D drawing. Three uniforms, values the game can set from outside. And line eight, the colour line from the spec, word for word. A shader is a small program the graphics card runs for every pixel the bar draws. This one takes the colour the bar arrived with, and mixes it toward orange.

beats.role_note: How game state reaches the shader: the driver (night_skip_driver.gd). Paired result B06 (motion + playtest + test timings).
beats.narration_text: So who sets skip amount during play? This driver. Each frame it reads the game state, and never writes it: fast forward, during the night phase. Move toward steps the value by delta, over a quarter second in, and half a second out. Then it hands the number to the material. Delta, not a frame count, so the fade takes the same time at thirty or a hundred forty-four frames a second.

props.title: How game state reaches the shader
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/ui/night_skip_driver.gd lines 20–28 · git bb2c156
props.code:
## The state the glow shows: the player is skipping the night (the HUD's own ">> x8" condition).
static func state_holds() -> bool:
	return LoopState.fast_forward and LoopState.phase == LoopState.Phase.NIGHT

func _process(delta: float) -> void:
	var target := 1.0 if state_holds() else 0.0
	var duration := FADE_IN if target > skip_amount else FADE_OUT
	skip_amount = move_toward(skip_amount, target, delta / duration)
	_apply()

beats.role_note: Q3 why a texture is information: hint_experiment.gdshader. Paired result B08.
beats.narration_text: Why is a texture information? This experiment binds one file, three grey texels, sixty-four, one twenty-eight and one ninety-two, to two samplers. One says source colour: these bytes are s R G B colour, so decode them. The other says nothing: these bytes are data. A bool picks which one writes albedo.

props.title: Same bytes, two meanings
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/shaders/hint_experiment.gdshader lines 5–15 · git bb2c156

beats.role_note: Result of B07: hint quads captured, with Shriram's prediction (CHANGE-BRIEF §2.5) and the measurement (TEST-REPORT A5.6).
beats.narration_text: Shriram predicted both quads before the shader existed. With the hint: sixty-four, one twenty-eight, one ninety-two, because the decode and the screen's encode cancel out. Without it: one thirty-seven, one eighty-eight, two twenty-five, encoded for the screen without ever being decoded. Captured: exactly those six numbers. Same bytes, different meaning.

beats.role_note: deck_marble.gdshader uniforms: colour vs data samplers, ranges, groups. Paired result B10.
beats.narration_text: The marble shader uses that difference. Albedo, the colour of the stone, gets source colour. Roughness and the normal map are data: no source colour, and the normal map says hint normal. Then five number uniforms, each with a range and a default, in two Inspector groups, surface and finish. Its UVs come from world X Z, so all four floors tile at the same scale.

props.title: Colour and data in one material

beats.role_note: Q2 material vs shader: marble_wet.tres. Paired result B12 (Shriram's editor checks A and B).
beats.narration_text: A shader is the program. A material is one set of values for it. Here's the wet material: the same shader file, the same three textures, and just two values changed, roughness zero point three, and specular zero point eight. The dry material sets none of them, so the shader's defaults apply.

props.title: A material is values for a shader
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/materials/marble_wet.tres lines 8–14 · git bb2c156

[resource]
shader = ExtResource("1_marble")
shader_parameter/albedo_tex = ExtResource("2_diff")
shader_parameter/roughness_tex = ExtResource("3_rough")
shader_parameter/normal_tex = ExtResource("4_nor")
shader_parameter/roughness_scale = 0.3
shader_parameter/specular_amount = 0.8

beats.role_note: Q4 the Godot shading language: standard_generated.gdshader (editor conversion). Paired result B14.
beats.narration_text: What is the Godot shading language? Shriram converted a standard material to code in the editor, and this is what Godot wrote. A shader type and a render mode up top. Then uniforms with hints, which build the Inspector: a colour for the albedo, and source colour on the albedo texture. It reads like G L S L, but Godot decides the stages and the built-ins.

beats.role_note: Two generated lines beside their equivalents in Shriram's shader (verbatim), annotated.
beats.narration_text: Line seven of the generated shader, beside line five of the marble shader: both put source colour on the albedo sampler. Line nineteen beside line eleven: Godot's normal map uses hint roughness normal, Shriram's uses hint normal, and neither decodes it as colour. That's what Godot's language adds over plain G L S L: shader types with their built-ins, and hints that wire each uniform to the Inspector and to colour decoding.

beats.role_note: The uniform-list assertion (test_night_skip.gd). Paired result B17 (mutations).
beats.narration_text: Now the tests. Setting a uniform and reading it back proves nothing, because Godot accepts any name without an error. So this test asks the compiled shader for its uniform list. An empty list means it failed to parse. A missing name means somebody renamed it.

props.title: Ask the shader, not a round trip
props.source: Godot editor reconstruction · godot/tests/test_night_skip.gd lines 83–90 · git bb2c156

beats.role_note: Result of B16: the three mutations' recorded output (logs/mutations/*.log), verbatim.
beats.narration_text: Shriram broke the shaders on purpose, three times. Delete one semicolon: a shader error, and four checks fail. Rename skip amount: two fail, while all twenty-two timing checks still passed, because the driver kept writing a name that no longer existed, silently. Remove source colour from the marble: the material test fails. Each run exited with one, and each file was restored.

beats.role_note: Agent mistakes caught; what no headless run can show; what remains uncertain.
beats.narration_text: What Claude and its agents got wrong, and how each was caught. The CLAUDE dot M D draft cited the wrong floor lines and missed two tests. The audit invented a colour temperature, misstated which floors share a material, and its hint check matched substrings, so source colour on a data sampler would have passed. An explicit assertion fixed that. The audit agent tried to reset project dot godot three times, and its scope denied it. And Claude first wrote its own curl formula, then replaced it with the course's. No headless run shows how anything looks. That's what the captures and Shriram's eyes are for.

props.title: What the agents got wrong
props.excerpt:
CLAUDE.md draft: wrong floor lines; 2 tests missing.
Audit: invented '~2700 K'; wrong on which floors share a material.
Audit test: substring hint check passed source_color on data → assertion added.
Audit agent: git checkout ×2 + git restore ×1 on project.godot → denied.
Claude: own curl formula → the course's.

beats.narration_text: Who did what. Shriram chose the state, the object, the colour, the fades and the marble, and made every prediction, with ChatGPT's help on the maths. Shriram typed in the night-skip shader; its colour line comes from the brief. Shriram wrote the marble and hint shaders with ChatGPT's help, learning shaders for the first time, from Claude's slot outline. Shriram ran the mutations and the human checks, and wrote the language notes in their own words; ChatGPT had paraphrased an earlier draft. Claude proposed options, organised the brief's prose, gave a slot outline for the Part 2 shaders, and wrote the driver, the tests, the wiring, the capture tools, the audit review, the docs and this film. Textures: Poly Haven's Marble zero one and Floor Tiles zero six, by Rob Tuytel, C C zero. Source revision, B B two C one five six.

beats.role_note: Verdict: checked / uncertain / limits / next.
beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. Checked: both shaders parse, the glow follows its rules at three frame rates, every predicted pixel held, and three mutations each failed their test. Uncertain: the marble's normal map is too flat for a decisive curl verdict, zero point six three seven. And the glow's on-screen contrast, three point four six to one, depends on the scene behind the bar. Next: Shriram's idea, a battery that drains from orange to red as dawn approaches.
